item.title: Hero VIP Club Fueled This Heartwarming Journey From Texas Shelters To Forever Homes
item.description:
On a warm morning in Clifton, Texas, rescuers crouched beside a house, peering into a dark crawlspace where a frightened mama dog and her puppies had taken shelter.

For days, the team from Bosque Animal Rescue Kennels (BARK) worked patiently to gain the family’s trust. At first, they could only catch one puppy at a time. Then another. Then another. Neighbors stepped in to help. Traps were carefully set. Food was left nearby. Slowly, the terrified little family began crossing what rescuers lovingly called the “safety threshold.”

And thanks to iHeartDogs customers and Hero VIP Club members, that frightened family’s story didn’t end underneath that house in Texas. Instead, it became the beginning of a brand-new life.

A Rescue Road Trip Fueled By Compassion

Earlier this month, iHeartDogs partnered once again with BARK Rescue in Clifton, Texas, to transport dozens of vulnerable dogs from overcrowded conditions in the South to rescue partners in Iowa and Wisconsin, where loving homes and foster families were waiting.

What started as a transport for 30 dogs quickly grew. More puppies needed help. Additional rescues stepped in. By the end of the back-to-back Rescue Road Trip weekends, 43 dogs had been safely transported north toward second chances.

Every mile of the journey was made possible by Hero VIP Club members and iHeartDogs supporters whose purchases help fund rescue transports, veterinary care, food, supplies, and lifesaving partnerships with shelters like BARK.

The Star Wars Puppies: Rescued One By One

Among the passengers was the now-famous “Star Wars litter,” seven puppies rescued from beneath the house alongside their exhausted mama dog.

Their rescue was anything but easy. The puppies darted back into the darkness while their nervous mother watched cautiously nearby. But rescuers refused to give up.

Eventually, with help from a compassionate neighbor who continued working with the family, the remaining puppies and their mama were safely brought into rescue care. One especially emotional moment came when the mother dog finally relaxed enough to fall asleep peacefully after arriving at BARK.

“We truly feel like she finally felt safe,” rescuers shared.

The puppies were later nicknamed the “Star Wars litter” in honor of their May 4th rescue date. It was the day these puppies finally enjoyed clean bedding, safety, and full bellies instead of hiding in fear under a house.

While their mama is still recovering from mastitis treatment, rescuers hope she’ll join a future Rescue Road Trip soon.

Conway: The Singing Texas Stray

Then there’s Conway. This one-year-old Beagle/Basset mix was found wandering alone in a remote Texas field before eventually making his way to a dog daycare facility, where staff contacted BARK for help.

Conway quickly became a favorite among rescuers thanks to his goofy personality and signature “singing” howl that earned him his country-music-inspired name.

And the best part? Not long after arriving in Iowa, Conway was adopted. After surviving alone in rural Texas, he now has the loving home every dog deserves.

Tiny Shrimp Stole Everyone’s Heart

Shrimp, the tiniest puppy on the transport, quickly became the unexpected star of the trip.  Abandoned with her litter on a county road before they were even weaned, Shrimp faced almost impossible odds from the very beginning. But rescuers described her as determined, sweet, and impossible not to love.

By the end of the trip, Shrimp stole the show, riding alongside rescuers and soaking up the cuddles as they rumbled down the road.

Echo’s Journey To Safety

Another passenger, Echo, had already survived unimaginable hardship before boarding the rescue van. According to BARK, Echo was dumped on a dirt road with his senior mother and eight siblings when he was only five weeks old and still nursing.

Without rescue intervention, puppies that young rarely survive long on their own. But Echo did survive. And this month, he climbed aboard the Rescue Road Trip van headed north toward a brighter future. And like Conway, he found his forever home in just a matter of days!

A Birthday Road Trip With Purpose

The journey north was documented by Alexis Sibila-Wellman, a BARK board member and Rescue Road Trip driver, who spent her birthday weekend transporting dogs to safety instead of celebrating herself.

Many of the pups were dressed up in party hats and posed with cakes in honor of Alexis, but like a true animal rescuer, her main concern was getting the job done.

“Thanks to y’all, we saved 43 dogs on a back-to-back weekend,” she said in a video message shared with iHeartDogs social media followers.

Every Purchase Helped Save These Dogs

Transporting dozens of dogs across multiple states requires fuel, veterinary clearances, crates, food, medications, rescue coordination, and countless hours from volunteers and shelter workers.

That’s where the iHeartDogs community stepped in. Because of Hero VIP Club members and customers who shop with purpose, dogs who once faced abandonment, neglect, and uncertainty were able to leave Texas behind for safety, foster homes, adoption events, and forever families waiting in Iowa and Wisconsin.

Some, like Conway and Echo, have already been adopted. Others are settling into foster homes and beginning the healing process. And many more now have the chance they never would have had otherwise.

Help Us Save The Next Batch of Rescue Road Trip Dogs

Every Rescue Road Trip proves something powerful: When compassionate people come together, lives change.

The Hero VIP Club helps fund lifesaving transports like this one while offering members exclusive perks, discounts, early access, and free shipping. But most importantly, membership helps rescue dogs in desperate situations get the second chance they deserve.

If you’re not already a Hero VIP Club member, now is the perfect time to join. Because somewhere tonight, another frightened mama dog is hiding with her puppies. Another dog is waiting alone on a dirt road. And with your help, more dogs can make the journey from survival to safety.

item.title: Top 8 Polyphenol-Rich Foods That Can Help Your Dog Fight Aging and Disease
item.description:

Polyphenols are natural compounds found in plant-based foods that pack powerful antioxidant and anti-inflammatory benefits. For dogs, a polyphenol-rich diet may help fight aging, reduce disease risk, and boost overall vitality. If you’re looking to give your pup a health advantage, these foods can offer a natural edge.

Blueberries

Blueberries are one of the richest sources of polyphenols and are known for their high levels of anthocyanins, which have powerful antioxidant effects. These little blue gems help neutralize free radicals in your dog’s body, supporting brain health, reducing inflammation, and even improving heart function. Studies have shown that dogs who regularly consume blueberries may experience slower cognitive decline as they age. You can add a few fresh blueberries to your dog’s meals or choose a topper that includes them, like the iHeartDogs Bone Broth & Collagen for Dogs, which combines antioxidant-rich ingredients for a delicious, health-boosting addition to your pup’s diet.

Spinach

Spinach is a green leafy vegetable that contains a variety of polyphenols, including flavonoids and phenolic acids. It’s also a great source of fiber, iron, and vitamins A, C, and K. These compounds work together to help support your dog’s immune system and may protect against certain types of cancer. You can lightly steam spinach and mix it into your dog’s food to make it more digestible and avoid any potential issues with oxalates.

Broccoli

Broccoli is another polyphenol powerhouse, packed with quercetin and kaempferol, both of which are known for their anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. Regular consumption may help protect your dog’s cells from oxidative damage and support detoxification processes. Broccoli can be served steamed or finely chopped raw in small quantities, as too much can cause digestive upset. Always monitor your dog when introducing cruciferous veggies.

Apples

Apples, particularly their skins, are rich in polyphenols like catechin and chlorogenic acid. These compounds can help manage blood sugar levels, reduce inflammation, and support a healthy gut microbiome. Apples also provide dietary fiber and vitamin C, making them a healthy and hydrating treat. Just be sure to remove the seeds and core before giving apples to your dog, as those parts can be toxic.

Carrots

Carrots are an excellent source of polyphenols and beta-carotene, which the body converts into vitamin A. This supports vision, skin, and immune health. Carrots also provide a crunchy, low-calorie snack for dogs and can be served raw or lightly cooked. Carrots pair well with blueberries in blends like the iHeartDogs Bone Broth & Collagen for Dogs, giving your dog a nutrient-dense boost in every bite.

Green Beans

Green beans are rich in flavonoids and other polyphenolic compounds that support healthy aging and reduce inflammation. They are also low in calories and high in fiber, which can help dogs feel full without adding extra weight. Green beans can be served cooked or raw, but be sure they are plain—without added salt, oils, or seasonings.

Sweet Potatoes

Sweet potatoes contain a wide range of polyphenols, including anthocyanins (especially in purple varieties), and are also a great source of dietary fiber and complex carbohydrates. They are excellent for gut health and can help regulate your dog’s digestion. The natural antioxidants in sweet potatoes support immune function and reduce the effects of aging. You can serve them steamed or baked and mashed into your dog’s meals.

Cranberries

Cranberries are loaded with polyphenols like proanthocyanidins, which can help prevent urinary tract infections and support a healthy gut. They also provide vitamin C, manganese, and other antioxidants that help keep your dog’s immune system strong. Fresh or dried cranberries (unsweetened and without additives) can be added to your dog’s food in small amounts, or you can look for them in high-quality dog treats and supplements.

Help Your Dog Thrive with Nature’s Antioxidants

Feeding your dog polyphenol-rich foods is a simple and effective way to support long-term health. These natural compounds help fight inflammation, oxidative stress, and age-related disease, making them a powerful ally in your pup’s wellness journey. Whether you’re adding fresh veggies and fruits or incorporating healthful toppers like the iHeartDogs Bone Broth & Collagen for Dogs, your dog will reap the rewards of a more vibrant, energized life. As a doting Doberman parent, your dog’s health is a top priority. You make sure your Doberman eats the best foods, gets regular veterinary care, enjoys plenty of playtime, and takes regular walks.

Gauging just how much activity your Doberman is getting can be difficult, though. But outfitting your best friend with one of the best dog activity trackers on the market can be beneficial in your quest to keep your pup their healthiest.

With a fitness tracker for your Doberman, you can monitor activity levels, track weight and nutrition, and even set daily fitness goals. Some trackers also come with GPS, so you always know your dog’s location. Plus, keeping track of your pup’s fitness and other health aspects can deepen your bond and increase your understanding of canine behavior.

But with so many options out there, choosing the best dog activity tracker can be tricky. Here are a few things to keep in mind when shopping for the tracker that best fits your needs.

Factors To Consider When Choosing Your Best Doberman Activity Tracker

Purpose

Their base reason for existence, fitness trackers are made to track your dog’s activity. But many of the choices on the market offer additional monitoring features for calorie burn, GPS-tracking, geofencing, and body composition, while even alerting you to a ramp-up in scratching and anxious behavior. But you may not need all those bells and whistles, so as you begin the search for your dog’s activity tracker, think about what health aspects you’d like to monitor.

Cost 

Dog activity trackers aren’t cheap. That’s why it’s essential to do your research and know just what you need from one. But remember this, just because a tracker is more expensive than others doesn’t automatically make it better than cheaper models. Also, check whether or not a tracker offers free services or if you’ll be committed to monthly subscriptions in order to use their services.  

Range and Connectivity

Always consider range and connectivity when shopping for the best dog activity tracker. If you’re buying for location monitoring or want geofencing options, you’ll most likely need to look at GPS-powered trackers. Plus, you’ll want to be aware of what interface a tracker uses to deliver data and alerts. Does it connect with your phone or smart home system? It’d be a bummer to get a tracker and realize it doesn’t work with the brand of your phone.

Size and Weight

This one’s pretty obvious; you don’t want to hang a huge and heavy tracker on your dog’s neck. Talk about uncomfortable! Be sure the tracker or tracker collar is lightweight and comfortable in fit. Rough material or hardware rubbing your pup’s neck is no fun for anyone! 

Battery Life

And don’t forget to look at battery life when shopping for the best dog activity tracker. In use 24/7, fitness trackers use major battery power, so look for a manufacturer’s battery information and read comments to see what users have to say about the time between charging. If you’re waffling between two tracker choices, let your deciding factor come down to battery life. Less charging means less worry over a dead tracker.

Now, after studying the field and keeping these considerations in mind, here are our picks for the best dog activity trackers!

Must-Have Activity Trackers for Active Dobermans

1. Tractive Smart GPS Activity Tracker

An advanced choice for tech-savvy pup parents, the Tractive Smart Dog GPS Tracker offers real-time location tracking with updates every 2 to 3 seconds and customizable virtual fences that alert you the moment your dog steps out of bounds. But this isn’t just about location, it’s about total well-being. Monitor your dog’s heart rate, respiratory health, and even barking behavior, right from your phone.

This collar-mounted device is lightweight, waterproof, and designed to stay secure on all your outdoor adventures. Like its predecessor, it requires a subscription plan (starting at $5 per month), but the added health insights may be worth every penny for those with curious roamers or senior dogs.

Pros

  • Live GPS tracking with instant alerts
  • Heart and respiratory rate monitoring
  • Bark detection and activity tracking
  • Waterproof and lightweight design
  • Works with any collar

Cons

  • Requires a monthly subscription
  • Advanced features may be more than casual users need

Using GPS and LTE-M cellular technology, it provides 24/7 location tracking, escape alerts, and activity monitoring. This makes it perfect for keeping tabs on dogs who love to roam. With a built-in LED light, waterproof construction, and tough hardware, it’s ready for everything from rainy hikes to late-night backyard zoomies.

This version includes a free 1-year membership, so you’re instantly connected and protected without extra setup costs. The bright yellow color adds visibility and flair, and the medium size fits most mid-sized pups.

  • Tracks activity and health metrics

Plus, it features a 3D accelerometer used by research institutions and vet schools to give you more precise activity monitoring. And because Fitbark works with your Fitbit, Apple Watch, Apple HealthKit, or Google Fit wearable device or smartphone, you and your pup can work out side-by-side and create a healthy lifestyle together.

More than just a lightweight and rugged activity tracker, it also monitors mobility, anxiety, and skin conditions through changes in the FitBark Health Index. The FitBark 2 provides up to 6 months of battery life, so you can worry less about recharging and more about bonding with your dog.

Pros

  • Waterproof and lightweight
  • Easy to set up
  • Strong battery life
  • 3D accelerometer for precise activity monitoring  
  • Links up to your fitness tracker

Cons

  • No GPS outside of the US

Compact and easy to use, the Cube GPS Tracker helps you monitor your dog’s location in real time using GPS technology and a connected app. Set custom safe zones with geo-fencing and receive alerts if your dog leaves the area. You can also ping the device on demand to check your dog’s location instantly. It’s small enough to fit comfortably on your dog’s collar and comes with a rechargeable battery for ongoing use.
